journal.title: Everett's claim of actual branches and why it is not a branch census
journal.intro: The 1957 primary paper explicitly treats every uncollapsed component as actual in the proposed theory. Its additive measure yields Born weights under assumptions; another theory with one actual configuration reproduces the same ordinary probabilities.

sections.heading: One wave function, multiple relative records
sections.text: A universal unitary quantum state can correlate observer memories with all relative outcomes. Everett's §5 proof-note says the components are all actual in that framework. The scientific question remains which ontology describes our actual physical universe.

sections.heading: Why additivity matters but does not finish probability
sections.text: Everett's positive additive measure yields squared-amplitude weights and typical repeated-memory records, but a measure on hypothetical branches does not alone prove their existence or why a particular observer should expect one future experience.

sections.heading: Next engineering and science work
sections.text: The roadmap's Truth Engine v0.2 requires data integrity, counterevidence, explicit score-change provenance and tests, while already implemented v0.25 reading rooms need acceptance revalidation. The planned scientific work is three parts for each part website development.

journal.title: Two histories of the same measurement?
journal.intro: Everett and Bohmian quantum equilibrium disagree about which histories physically exist while agreeing on standard experimental frequencies.

sections.heading: Ontology is not automatically an observable
sections.text: Everett's unitary global wave has multiple branch-relative records. Bohmian mechanics assigns one actual guided particle configuration. Given quantum equilibrium, both yield the same Born measurement statistics.

sections.heading: Where predictions really can differ
sections.text: GRW and CSL change the physical dynamics. Size and time-dependent loss of interference or spontaneous X-ray emission may constrain a specified localization mechanism; environmental decoherence is a major alternative that must be calibrated.

sections.heading: A measured constraint, not a parallel-universe photograph
sections.text: March 2026 XENONnT 1–140 keV results constrain particular Markovian CSL/DP parameter choices. Bell tests constrain locality assumptions. Neither measures the number of actually real Everett branches.

sections.heading: Our open conclusion
sections.text: Three newly completed full original-main-text critical reviews bring the indexed completed total to 13 of 400. The objective is scientific discrimination, not a higher review count; VC-008 leaves 59/100 as an inherited editorial orientation, not a probability.

journal.category: FULL-SOURCE RESEARCH · R006 · TEN COMPLETE STUDIES
journal.title: Ten full scientific reviews: what original research establishes about timelines
journal.intro: The first ten critical main-text source studies are complete. Their conclusions constrain local hidden-variable theories, wavefunction ontology, chronology horizons, quantum causal operations and inflationary bubble detection—but none directly counts real quantum branches.

sections.heading: The main milestone: 10 of 400 full-source reviews
sections.text: We studied whole original main publications or the complete scholarly entry, and logged their sections, methods, assumptions, limitations, independent checks and competing explanations. Nine previously indexed works and one new single-world paper were promoted; no abstract-only work was relabeled merely to raise the counter.

sections.heading: 1. Bell and PBR: strong theorems, narrow conclusions
sections.text: Bell's 1964 original demonstrates the nonlocality constraint on precise preassignment models. PBR's full paper and appendices restrict overlapping ψ-epistemic descriptions under independent preparation. Neither theorem asserts that Everettian branches were directly observed.

sections.heading: 2. Many-worlds theory alongside a substantive single-world response
sections.text: Vaidman's full 2026 scholarly treatment explains branch ontology, Born-weight and preferred-basis objections. Lazarovici and Hubert's complete rebuttal addresses a Wigner's-friend paradox using Bohmian definite particle configurations and still-live empty wave branches. They disagree about ontology and do not provide a new branch detector.

sections.heading: 3. Quantum causal order and a Bell-Wigner experiment
sections.text: Oreshkov's process-matrix paper yields a theoretical causal-inequality violation. Procopio's optical quantum switch demonstrates a controlled ordering advantage; Proietti's six-photon Bell-Wigner experiment violates an observer-independent-facts inequality with explicit fair-sampling and observer-definition limitations. These different results must never be counted as direct observation of parallel physical timelines.

sections.heading: 4. Cosmology, rotating metrics and time-loop formation
sections.text: Feeney's complete five-page WMAP analysis uses matched simulations and Bayesian evidence to constrain detectable bubble collisions. Gödel's four-page paper constructs an exact rotating metric with closed timelike circles. Hawking's full original paper investigates restrictions on manufactured chronology horizons. None is evidence for quantum branching in our actual universe.

sections.heading: Math checks and what remains unverified
sections.text: Limited independent checks included CHSH singlet 2√2, PBR two-qubit exclusion orthogonality, Gödel's radius asinh(1), the causal-success value (2+√2)/4, and Proietti's reported significance. Entire experimental datasets, external appendices and full general-relativistic tensor calculations were not independently reproduced. Complete details, source URLs and caveats are in research/full-study-batch-001.md.

sections.heading: The empirical verdict did not move
sections.text: Our central question remains unresolved: one experienced outcome is not an experimental count of all physically real histories. The inherited 59/100 meter is an editorial display rather than calibrated posterior. Research audit VC-007 records 59 to 59 with zero evidential branch-count shift. Next, work on original Everett and Bohm papers, objective-collapse experimental constraints and a quantitative discrimination matrix.

journal.category: RESEARCH REPORT · R005 · ONE REAL HISTORY OR MANY
journal.title: Does our universe contain one timeline—or many physically real histories?
journal.intro: The central problem is the number of actual outcome histories in our own universe, not whether people can revisit the past.

sections.heading: 1 · Everett and relative-state branches
sections.text: Everett interprets one universal uncollapsed quantum state as encompassing many branch-relative worlds. No other actual branch has been directly counted. SRC-007, SRC-012, NOTE-026.

sections.heading: 2 · Decoherence and the quantum cat
sections.text: Environmental entanglement suppresses locally visible interference but does not decide whether a single outcome or multiple branch-relative histories are physically actual. SRC-011, SRC-058, NOTE-027.

sections.heading: 3 · Bohm's one actual configuration
sections.text: Nonlocal particle guidance assigns definite actual positions while reproducing many quantum results, showing that generic interference alone does not demand many actual histories. SRC-010, SRC-059, NOTE-028.

sections.heading: 4 · GRW collapse and molecular experiments
sections.text: Physical-collapse modifications have parameter-dependent predictions. Large-molecule quantum interference constrains some, not all, modified models. SRC-042, SRC-048, NOTE-029.

sections.heading: 5 · Bell tests do not count timelines
sections.text: Loophole-free Bell experiments reject specified local-realist models, not nonlocal single-outcome physics as a category or Everett-vs-Bohm ontology. SRC-060, SRC-061, NOTE-030.

sections.heading: 6 · Separate cosmological bubble hypotheses
sections.text: Eternal-inflation bubbles are physically different from Everett branches. WMAP bubble-collision data showed no warrant for additional model complexity under the tested scenario. SRC-062, SRC-063, NOTE-031.

sections.heading: 7 · PBR's narrower conclusion
sections.text: Wavefunction ontic-status constraints under preparation independence do not prove many actual histories. SRC-044, NOTE-032.

sections.heading: Verdict and continuation
sections.text: One observed history is consistent with competing ontologies. No decisive physical history-count experiment; editorial compass stays 59→59, VC-006. More detailed mathematical and experimental comparisons are next.

journal.title: What chronology protection actually proves—and what it cannot yet prove
journal.intro: A rigorous quantum-field theorem can show that a mathematical description breaks down at specified horizon points without establishing what complete quantum gravity will do.

sections.heading: Hawking's bounded-region scenario
sections.text: Hawking's local construction analysis concerns compactly generated Cauchy horizons, geometric energy conditions and semiclassical vacuum polarization. The backreaction conclusion remains a conditional physical conjecture; it does not eliminate every imaginable closed timelike path.

sections.heading: The precise Kay–Radzikowski–Wald result
sections.text: For a linear field on a spacetime with a compactly generated horizon, specified base points obstruct the usual F-local field algebra and regular Hadamard two-point extension. Even where stress looks bounded before the horizon, the limiting quantum field description can become ill-defined at those base points.

sections.heading: Visser's reliability objection
sections.text: Visser argues semiclassical gravity can cease to be trustworthy because of Planck-scale metric fluctuations before a chronology horizon; a Roman-ring toy geometry also challenges reliance on universally large mean stress. Neither result creates physical time travel.

sections.heading: Evidence verdict
sections.text: The experimental question remains open. This theoretical comparison does not independently detect backward travel or discriminate single-history and many-histories ontology. The site's illustrative 59/100 editorial score stays unchanged; see field-note-003, SOURCE-055–057 and audit VC-005.

journal.title: The problem is not the grandfather. It is the meaning of a history.
journal.intro: The grandfather paradox is a warning against combining incompatible assumptions. It is not evidence that the cosmos forks.

sections.heading: Three distinct questions
sections.text: Can a clock traverse time at a different rate? Can a physical observer return to an earlier event? If quantum theory branches, are these branches independent histories? The first is experimentally supported; the others remain open.

sections.heading: An evidence discipline
sections.text: A mathematical solution is not a physical device. A quantum simulation is not a journey to yesterday. A philosophical interpretation is not an observation of parallel timelines.

sections.heading: Our research standard
sections.text: Every claim is connected to a dated source, an evidence category, a relevance judgment and a clearly stated limitation. Only findings that distinguish competing accounts can move an empirical verdict.
